analysis.title: The Speculative Grade Beat: Good Time Market's Got the Blues
key_insights: Citi says the credit cycle is turning more negative. The two remaining supports, the AI buildout and a light regulatory touch, may be shifting after Tuesday's midterm elections. If either is compromised, Citi would become more cautious on credit risk.

Citi forecasts year-end 2027 default rates of 4.5% for high yield bonds and 8.1% for leveraged loans. The two markets' distress ratios both rose this year, but the sources of distress differ, so the surface-level ratio is less reliable for the forecast.

High yield distress ratio (par share of CCC bonds trading below $60) is 33.7%, above the pandemic level and the highest since the early-2016 energy crash. Citi argues it overstates default risk because the stress is concentrated.

Half of all distressed high yield par comes from nine large issuers in the first and second size quartiles. More than half of distress below $60 comes from Media/Communications, and six of the nine large issuers are media names.

The CCC segment has shrunk in the Bloomberg High Yield Index from 11-14% historically to below 10% this year. The share of unique issuers trading below $60 is lower than at the December 2022 peak, even though the par-weighted CCC distress ratio is higher. Default rates are issuer-weighted, which supports a lower default forecast.

Citi expects high yield stress to resolve mostly through liability management exercises (LMEs) and M&A or divestitures rather than hard defaults, which supports recovery assumptions for bonds relative to loans.

Loan distress ratio (share of loans trading below $80) is 8.0%, far below major stress periods and comparable to December 2022, when the default rate 12 months later was 5.8%. Citi says loans have diverged from this signal because LMEs hit otherwise non-distressed credits, but expects the ratio to regain predictive power next year as the LME share of stress declines.

$80B of loans in the Citi Leveraged Loan Tracker mature within two years, and a third of that trades below $90. That is 2.3% of the Tracker, the highest since Citi began tracking, and Citi says it signals more acute stress than the 8.0% distress ratio.
Loan stress is broadening to smaller issuers. The Morningstar/LSTA Index distress ratio of 8.0% compares with 5.8% for the Tracker (loans of $1B or larger), the widest gap since the pandemic.

Software's share of loan distress fell from 60% in March to 40% as the overall distress ratio rose from 5.3% to 5.6%, so stress is now emerging from nearly all sectors. Software remains the largest contributor and AI-driven disruption remains a key concern.

Citi recently shifted its asset allocation in favor of high yield over loans. The default forecasts add conviction, and Citi expects more benign spread widening and default losses in high yield than in loans.

Credit spreads remain tight despite the recent backup. October had the most triple-C issuers falling at least 10% in a month since 2022, and the pattern is broadening to single-B issuers. Citi says broad risk aversion is now the main driver of triple-C spreads.

Fed expectations turned hawkish in spring because of inflation tied to the Iran conflict and the AI buildout. The implied Dec-27 Fed funds rate went from about 3% in late 2025 to nearly 5% in September and is now 4.3%. Long Treasury yields hit multi-decade highs driven by real yields.

Higher real yields let investors earn compelling inflation-adjusted returns without reaching down in quality, which keeps leveraged finance spreads tight. BBB-rated hyperscaler spreads have widened to levels comparable to a high yield bellwether, which Citi reads as some funding stress.

Primary market activity has been robust. Investment grade supply is up 25% year to date versus last year's non-pandemic record. High yield supply is roughly unchanged, and the market absorbed $54bn of AI-related supply and the two largest dollar-denominated deals on record.

Citi sees the post-election market swings as likely reflecting positioning. Divided government should help vol suppression and legislative gridlock, but may shift the AI buildout and regulatory support.

sector_views.sector: High yield bonds vs leveraged loans
sector_views.rationale: Citi recently shifted its allocation toward high yield over loans. It expects more benign spread widening and default loss in high yield, while loan defaults are forecast to be much higher.
The sector accounts for more than half of high yield par trading below $60 and is in secular decline. Citi expects LME-type restructurings rather than hard defaults.
Software is the largest contributor to loan distress, driven by concerns over AI-related disruption, though its share of distress has fallen from 60% to 40% as other sectors weaken.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A modest rise, below what the 33.7% distress ratio would imply, because distress is concentrated in about nine large issuers and Media/Communications.
More severe than the 8.0% distress ratio implies, driven by the maturity wall, smaller issuers and AI disruption of software, with fewer defaults absorbed by LMEs.

tension_points.bull_case: The AI buildout and a light regulatory touch have kept the cycle expanding. IG supply is up 25% year to date, and high yield absorbed $54bn of AI supply plus the two largest dollar deals on record.
tension_points.bear_case: Idiosyncratic weakness is spreading, October had the most CCC issuers falling 10%+ since 2022, hyperscaler spreads have widened to HY-like levels, and the midterm results may shift the AI buildout and regulatory support.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Citi says it would become more cautious on credit risk if the AI buildout or the light regulatory touch is compromised.

tension_points.bull_case: High yield distress is concentrated in about nine large issuers and Media/Communications, and mostly resolves through LMEs, so defaults rise only to 4.5% by year-end 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Loan stress is broadening across smaller issuers and nearly all sectors, with a record share of near-term maturities below $90, pointing to 8.1% defaults by year-end 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Citi expects the loan distress ratio to regain predictive power as the LME share of stress declines. A continued high LME share would weaken that case.

theme_stances.key_argument: High yield distress is concentrated in a few large issuers and one sector, while loan stress is broadening and the maturity wall is approaching.
theme_stances.evidence: half of all distressed par comes from just nine large issuers

theme_stances.key_argument: The mixed backdrop for the credit cycle is turning more negative, and the AI buildout and light regulation supports are critical to credit expansion.
theme_stances.evidence: The two remaining supports, AI buildout and a light regulatory touch
